implementation of the order dated 09.01.2019. High
Court, by its order dated 07.11.2022, directed the
Bangalore Development Authority to comply with the
directions within 3 months. Given that no action was
taken, respondents filed a Contempt Petition CCC No.
785/2023, wherein the Division Bench held that there
was sufficient ground to proceed with framing of
charges against the appellant herein. The present

--- Page 378 ---
2
appeal is against this order of the High Court dated
09.07.2025.
4. We are informed that pending disposal of this
appeal, Bangalore Development Authority has filed a
writ appeal, which was taken up and disposed of by the
Division Bench of the High Court by its order dated
20.08.2025.  The relevant portion of the order is
reproduced hereunder :-
“5.  Prima  facie,  the  operative
directions issued by the learned Single
Judge  can  be  construed  only  as
direction to the appellants to allot
sites  to  those  persons  who  are
otherwise  eligible  and  entitled  for
such allotment.  
6.The learned counsel for appellants
seeks to withdraw the present appeal
with liberty to file an application for
clarification before the learned Single
Judge.  The appeal is dismissed with
the above liberty.”
  
5. Ms. Kiran Suri, learned senior counsel appearing
for the appellants, has brought to our notice that
pursuant to the directions of the Division Bench, the
Bangalore  Development  Authority  has  also  filed  a
Review Petition, which is said to be pending disposal.
6. In  view  of  above  development,  while  the
appellants pursue their remedies, the Division Bench
hearing the contempt petition may not proceed till the

--- Page 379 ---
3
Review Petition is taken up and disposed of by the
concerned Bench.
7. With this clarification, the appeal is disposed
of.

is/are disposed of.

VERSUS
CHALASANI RAHUL                 RESPONDENT(S)
ORDER
1. The parties in-person are present and are
duly represented by their respective counsel.
2. The substantive matter in this Court is for
transferring the case bearing M.C. No. 127 of 2025,
titled “ Rahul  Chalasani  Vs.  Sriramaneni  Pujitha ”
from the Court of Senior Civil Judge, Bangalore
Rural  District  at  Bangalore,  Karnataka  to  the
Family Court at Tirupathi, Andhra Pradesh.
3. The parties, with the intervention of well-
wishers, as stated before us, have entered into a
settlement, agreed to dissolve their marriage, and
to quash/withdraw various cases pending between
them before different Courts. To that effect, the
Settlement Agreement dated 31.08.2026 is entered
into and placed on record.
4. In terms of the aforesaid settlement, the
parties have moved an application under Section 13-
B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 read with Article
142 of the Constitution of India, bearing I.A. No.

--- Page 386 ---
2
265045/2026,  seeking  dissolution  of  marriage
between the parties by a decree of divorce on the
basis of mutual consent.
5. As set out in Clause 10.1 read with 10.3 of
the Settlement Agreement, the respondent, during
and in the course of the hearing, has discharged
the primary obligation of paying the amount. The
petitioner receives the amount and acknowledges the
same. The parties have agreed to quash or withdraw
the cases pending between them in different courts.
6. For  the  reasons  stated  therein  and
considering  the  circumstances  of  the  case,  we
consider  it  a  fit  case  for  exercising  our
jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution
of India.
7. Hence, I.A. No. 265045/2026 is allowed. We
allow  the  parties'  prayer  to  dissolve  their
marriage by mutual consent.
8. There shall be a decree of divorce by mutual
consent  between  the  petitioner,  ‘Sriramaneni
Pujitha’, and the respondent, ‘Chalasani Rahul’, in
terms  of  the  settlement,  and  the  parties  are
directed to abide by the terms of the settlement.
The cases referred to in paragraphs ‘6.1’ and ‘6.2’
of  the  settlement  are  either  dismissed  or
withdrawn, as the case may be.

--- Page 387 ---
3
9. Let a decree to this effect be drawn up
accordingly.
10. The  present  application,  being  I.A.  No.
265045/2026,  and  the  transfer  petition  stand
disposed of in the above terms.
11. The  settlement  arrived  at  between  the
parties shall be made part of the order of even
date.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand
disposed of.

For Respondent(s) :Mr. Ramesh Babu, Sr. Adv.

    Mr. Sashwat Mishra, Adv.

    Mr. Abid Ali Beeran P., AOR
    Mr. Saswat Adhyapak, Adv.
    Ms. Namita Kumari, Adv. 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We heard Mr. Basant R., the learned senior counsel
appearing for the petitioner-accused and on the other hand,
Mr. Ramesh Babu, the learned senior counsel appearing for
1

--- Page 407 ---
the State. We also heard Mr. Nikhil Goel, the learned senior
counsel appearing for the complainant.
2. It appears from the materials on record that the Chief
Conservator  of  Forests  (Northern  Circle)  constituted  a
Special Investigation Team (SIT) to investigate into the
allegations  levelled  against  the  petitioner  insofar  as
collection  of  timber  and  selling  the  same  to  the
complainant.
3. The Special Investigation Team, at the end of the
investigation  found  that  the  petitioner  had  failed  to
maintain mandatory records, including stock purchase and
sales registers, and that the timber had been illegally
felled from forest land and transported using fabricated
documents. These are the allegations levelled in the FIR
lodged by the Forest Department for the offence punishable
under Section 27(1)(d)(e)(iii)(iv), 40, 39, 52 and 61A of
the Kerala Forest Act, 1961, respectively and Rules 12 and
23  of  the  Kerala  Forest  Produce  Transit  Rules,  1975,
respectively (for short, “The Rules, 1975”).
4. Simultaneously, it appears that the complainant also
lodged an FIR for the offence punishable under Section 420
of the IPC on the premise that he had been cheated by the
petitioner-accused by supplying him with illegally felled
timber.
5. Short point now that arises is whether both the cases
should be tried simultaneously by one particular Court or
not.
2

--- Page 408 ---
6. We are of the view that since offences relating to the
Forest Act are to be tried by a Special Court, let the case
arising from the FIR lodged by the complainant also be tried
by that very same court, however, one after the other.
Evidence shall be recorded separately in both the cases.
7. The Judicial First Class Magistrate, Chottanikkara,
Ernakulam, Kerala shall transfer Criminal Case being CC
No.456  of  2022  to  the  Court  of  Judicial  First  Class
Magistrate, Sulthan, Bathery, Wayanad, Kerala.
8. With the aforesaid, the Special Leave Petition stands
disposed of.
9. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  also  stand
disposed of.
(HARPREET KAUR)                                 (POOJA SHARMA)
COURT MASTER (SH)                             COURT MASTER (NSH)

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The appellant in First Appeal From Order No.
1011 of 2026 before the High Court is the special
leave petitioner.
2. The special leave petition challenges the
interim order dated 24.04.2026, particularly the
direction contained in paragraph Nos. ‘9’ and ‘10’,

--- Page 422 ---
2 SLP(C) No. 25210/2026
which read as under:
“9. Until further orders of this Court,
the effect and operation of the award dated
30.12.2025 passed by the Motor Accident
Claim Tribunal, Ghazipur in M.A.C.T. No. 55
of 2022 (Smt. Savita Devi and others Versus
Uttar  Pradesh  State  Road  Transport
Corporation  and  others)  shall  remain
stayed,  provided  the  appellant  deposits
entire amount awarded by the Tribunal along
with upto date interest before the Tribunal
within six weeks from today.
10. The Tribunal shall release the 50%
of the amount deposited by the appellant
under this order in favour of the claimants
immediately on filing of an application by
them,  without  asking  for  any
security/surety. Share of minor claimants)
(if  any),  shall  be  invested  in  fixed
deposit  scheme  till  he/she/they  would
attain majority.”
3. This Court has issued limited notice for
deciding whether the respondents are required to
furnish security while withdrawing the 50 per cent
allowed  to  be  withdrawn  by  the
respondents/claimants.
4. We have heard the learned counsel appearing
for the parties.
5. We are of the view that the conditions in
paragraph Nos. 9 to 11 are modified as under:
The petitioner is directed to deposit 25
per cent of the amount awarded together
with interest within four (04) weeks from

--- Page 423 ---
3 SLP(C) No. 25210/2026
today. The respondents are permitted to
withdraw  the  amount  deposited  by  the
petitioner without furnishing security. 
6. There shall be stay of the Award subject to
complying with the above directions.
7. The special leave petition stands disposed
of in the above modified terms.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand
disposed of.

Date : 22-09-2026 This matter was called for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE  MR. JUSTICE PRASANNA B. VARALE
                           [IN CHAMBER]

For Respondent(s) : 
  O R D E R
Vide order dated 20.02.2026, the learned Chamber Judge
was  not  inclined  to  consider  the  application  seeking
exemption from surrendering and, while dismissing the said
application,  granted  eight  (08)  weeks'  time  to  the
petitioner to surrender.
Thereafter, when the matter was listed on 06.05.2026,
learned counsel brought to the notice of the Court that the
petitioner was abroad and, on account of a war situation,
was  unable  to  travel.  Though  not  convinced  with  the
1

--- Page 440 ---
submission made on behalf of the petitioner, the learned
Chamber Judge granted indulgence as a last chance by
extending the time to surrender by four (04) weeks.
Paragraph No.4 of the order dated 06.05.2026 reads as
under:
“ 4.  However,  as  a  last  chance  further  period  of  four
weeks  from  today  is  granted  to  the  petitioner,  within
which time the applicant shall invariably surrender. If
the  petitioner  fails  to  surrender  within  the  time
indicated  above,  a  strict  view  will  be  taken,  and  the
consequences in law shall follow. ”
Today, learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently
submitted that due to personal and financial difficulties,
the  petitioner  was  unable  to  surrender  within  the
stipulated period and prayed that at least one (01) week's
further time be granted to surrender. However, apart from
this oral submission, there is nothing on record to show
any reason beyond the control of the petitioner making him
unable to surrender within the extended period of four (04)
weeks.
In view thereof, I am not inclined to grant any further
extension to the petitioner and the request for extension
of time to surrender is accordingly declined.
The petitioner shall surrender immediately, failing
which  the  authority  concerned  shall  take  steps  for
apprehending him.
Post the matter before the Court after two (02) weeks.
2

--- Page 441 ---
The Registry shall communicate a copy of this order to
all concerned forthwith.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The Order passed by this Court on 12-9-2023, the violation of
which is alleged, reads thus:-
“On the last date, we have heard the learned counsel
for the parties on merits and we found that this is not a
case to interfere under Article 136 of the Constitution of
India.  However,  we  did  not  dismiss  the  Special  Leave
Petition on the last date with a view to enable the learned
counsel for the petitioners to take instructions whether
the petitioners want time to vacate the suit premises. 

--- Page 449 ---
2
On the prayer made by the learned counsel appearing for
the petitioners, we are inclined to grant time of one year
to vacate the suit premises. Special Leave Petition is
dismissed.  However,  the  petitioners  shall  not  be
dispossessed  till  30th  September,  2024,  subject  to
condition of all the petitioners filing undertakings on
oath before this Court within a period of one month from
today  stating  that  they  will  vacate  and  handover  the
property subject matter of this Special Leave Petition to
the respondent on or before 30th September, 2024 and that
they will not part with possession of the property and will
not create any third party interests therein. 
We make it clear that on the failure of the petitioners
to file the undertakings within a period of one month from
today,  the  concession  granted  to  the  petitioners  for
vacating the property within one year will stand withdrawn.
The learned counsel for the petitioners will serve copies
of  the  undertakings  to  the  learned  counsel  for  the
respondent. 
Needless to add that the petitioners will continue to
pay the agreed rent till the date of vacating the suit
premises. 
With the above observations, the Special Leave Petition
is dismissed. 
Pending applications stand disposed of.”
2. Thus, the Respondents – the alleged Contemnors, were granted
time to vacate and hand over the possession of the suit premises on
or before 30th September, 2024. In this regard, they also filed
their undertaking on oath. It is not in dispute that the possession
was handed over on 30th September, 2024 as undertaken by them. 
3. However, the grievance of the petitioner today is that only a
portion of the property was handed over and further a  wall has
been constructed, and in such circumstances, the respondents cannot
be said to have duly complied with their undertaking. 
4. What has been pointed out to us today is a highly disputed
question of fact. It is difficult for us to adjudicate what has
been stated in the Contempt Petition as regards construction of
wall, etc. If there is any other grievance at the end of the
petitioner  to  redress,  it  shall  be  open  for  him  to  avail
appropriate legal remedy before the appropriate forum in accordance

--- Page 450 ---
3
with law including filing of a Civil Suit.
5. With the aforesaid, this petition stands disposed of.
6. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
 (VISHAL ANAND)                                  (POOJA SHARMA)
DEPUTY REGISTRAR                               COURT MASTER(NSH)

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. IA No. 202660 of 2026 is moved for suspension of
sentence and grant of bail to appellant No.1 - Ravindra
Singh, on the ground that similarly placed co-appellants,
namely Shailendra Singh and Narendra Singh, have already
been granted bail vide order dated 13.07.2026, and the case
of the appellant No.1 - Ravindra Singh is similar.
2. Mr. Babul Kumar, learned counsel appearing for the
legal heirs of the deceased victim, would submit that the
appellant No.1 - Ravindra Singh has earlier misused liberty
and has also threatened the son of the deceased. Therefore,
he is not entitled to be released on bail.
3. Having heard learned counsel for the parties, we are
of the considered view that appellant No. 1 - Ravindra
Singh, aged 72 years, deserves to be released on bail for
the reason that co-appellants Shailendra Singh, aged 77
years, and Narendra Singh, aged 76 years, were released on
bail on the ground of their age and incarceration for about
9 years and more.
4. Appellant No.1 - Ravindra Singh has also suffered
more than 9 years of jail sentence (with remission) and he
is also aged about 72 years. It is also to be seen that the
main accused Jai Deo Singh has already been granted pardon
by Hon’ble Governor of the State of Uttar Pradesh.
5. Accordingly, we direct that the sentence imposed
2

--- Page 453 ---
upon  appellant  No.1  -  Ravindra  Singh,  shall  remain
suspended and he shall be released on bail pending hearing
of this appeal, subject to such terms and conditions as may
be imposed by the trial court.
6. IA No. 202660/2026 is allowed. 
7. Considering the apprehension raised by the son of
the deceased victim, we further direct that appellant No.1
- Ravindra Singh shall mark his appearance before the
concerned police station between 11:00 AM to 1:00 PM on the
first Monday of every month during pendency of this appeal,
and he shall not indulge in any other criminal activity.
8. List the appeal for hearing in due course.

                             O R D E R
1. The present case, prima facie, appears to be a case
where the injured eye-witness, PW-2, Lachram Premi, has
categorically deposed that the petitioner was the person
who  shot  dead  two  of  his  colleagues  and  also  caused
injuries to him. The other evidence also establishes the
crime committed by the petitioner.
1

--- Page 497 ---
2. In the present case, the Trial Court has awarded
rigorous imprisonment for life, i.e., imprisonment for the
remainder of the petitioner's natural life, for the offence
punishable under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860
(for  short  ‘IPC’).  The  petitioner  has  further  been
sentenced to imprisonment for a period of ten years for the
offence  punishable  under  Section  307  of  the  IPC,  in
relation to the shooting of Lachram Premi. The petitioner
has also been sentenced to imprisonment for life for the
offence punishable under Section 27(3) of the Arms Act,
1959.
3. Though we do not find any substance or merit in the
present petition insofar as the conviction is concerned, we
consider it appropriate to issue limited notice solely on
the question of the quantum of sentence.
4. Mr. Siddharth Luthra, learned Senior Counsel, is
appointed as  Amicus  Curiae  to assist the Court in the
matter.
5. The Registry is directed to issue notice to the
respondent-State, confined to the limited question of the
quantum of sentence.
6. The  Registry  is  further  directed  to  furnish  a
complete set of the paper books/record to the learned
Amicus  Curiae as well as to the learned Standing Counsel
appearing for the State of Chhattisgarh.
7. The respondent-State of Chhattisgarh is directed to
2

--- Page 498 ---
file its reply before the next date of hearing.
8. List the matter after four weeks.

24.07.2026 passed by this Court, both the appellants have

the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-State of
PETITION(S) FOR SPECIAL LEAVE TO APPEAL (CRL.)  NO(S).  9825/2026

--- Page 530 ---
2
Uttar Pradesh. In the present case, appellant No.1 is aged
about 83 years, while appellant No.2 is aged about 68
years. The incident occurred in the year 1983, and both the
appellants, during the course of the trial, had undergone
incarceration for five and a half years and six years,
respectively.
3.  Learned counsel for the appellants has argued before
this Court that there is lot of contradiction and omission
and there is every possibility of them succeeding in the
criminal appeal and, therefore, keeping in view the fact
they were on bail during the trial and also keeping in view
the fact that they are of advance age, the application for
suspension of sentence deserves to be allowed.
4.  On  the  other  hand,  learned  counsel  for  the
respondent-State has vehemently opposed the prayer for
grant of bail and suspension of sentence. He has placed
reliance on the statement of PW1, PW2, PW4 and PW5 and he
has stated that the appellants have rightly been held
guilty by the Trial Court as well as of the High Court for
offences punishable under Section 302 read Section 34 of
the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
5. This court after hearing learned counsel for the
parties and after going through the record is of the
opinion that the application for suspension of sentence
deserves to be allowed and it is accordingly allowed.
Ordered accordingly.

and Haryana at Chandigarh in LPA No.2887 of 2025 (O&M) by which,
the judgment dated 12.05.2025 passed by the learned Single Judge of
the High Court in Writ Petition No.3117 of 2001 setting aside the
Award dated 08.05.1998 passed by the Industrial Tribunal, Punjab,

--- Page 744 ---
2
Chandigarh  in  Reference  No.67  of  1996  directing  payment  of
Rs.1,42,000/-(Rupees One Lakh Forty Two Thousand) to the petitioner
along with interest thereon, on account of difference of wages, has
been upheld basically on the ground that Section 33-C(2) of the
Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 cannot be maintained directly by way
of an adjudication proceedings in the absence of there being an
adjudication or an Award passed by the Competent Authority/Court.
5. We find that the grounds on which the appeal has been declined
to be entertained by the High Court, cannot be faulted in law.
6. Accordingly, we do not find any merit in the present petition
and the same stands disposed of.
7. However, it shall be open to the petitioner to move before the
appropriate forum for seeking reference of the dispute. If the
petitioner moves the appropriate forum within four weeks from
today, such reference would be decided in accordance with law by
the forum concerned expeditiously, preferably, within three months
from the date of reference being made.
8. On the reference being made to the Tribunal/Court concerned,
the  same  shall  be  considered  and  finally  decided  by  the
Tribunal/Court concerned, within nine months from the date of such
reference.
9. We clarify that we have not expressed any opinion on the
merits of the matter.
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.

Special Leave Petition, we had directed the petitioner
to deposit 7,00,000/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Only) before₹
the Trial Court with a further direction to the Trial
1

--- Page 1026 ---
Court to invest the said amount in a fixed deposit in a
Nationalized  Bank  with  auto-renewal  facility.  The
deposit was directed to be made within a period of two
weeks.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that when
the applicant had approached the Trial Court/Execution
Court at Jaipur for the deposit, he was told that the
execution proceedings have been transferred from the
Execution Court at Jaipur to the City Civil Court at
Chennai. In such circumstances, the Court at Jaipur
expressed its inability to accept the deposit.
4. In the circumstances, prayer has been made to allow
the applicant to deposit the amount directed by this
Court on 10.08.2026 before the Registry of this Court.
5. We allow the present Interlocutory Application and
permit the applicant/petitioner to deposit 7,00,000/-₹
(Rupees Seven Lakhs Only) before the Registry of this
Court within a period of two weeks from today which
shall be invested in a fixed deposit with auto-renewal
facility in a Nationalized Bank.
6. IA is accordingly disposed of.
7. List the Special Leave Petition on 17.11.2026 to
enable the respondents to file counter affidavit.
8. Interim order dated 10.08.2026, shall continue.

--- Page 1212 ---
(Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 in respect of grant of

matter back to the Special Judge.

case, this Court had granted protection while disposing of the
earlier Special Leave Petition, the petitioner should not be made
to suffer only for a procedural lapse.

Qureshi, AOR.
